synopsis: A successful New York advertising executive must raise his young son alone after his wife abruptly leaves the family. The film follows their evolving bond before a bitter custody battle forces them to fight for their future together.

During the Vietnam War, a U.S. Army captain is sent on a secret mission deep into the jungle to assassinate a rogue Special Forces colonel who has gone mad with power. A harrowing odyssey into the heart of darkness and human savagery.

A driven Broadway choreographer and director reflects on his glamorous yet self-destructive life through a series of fantasy sequences as he faces a major heart operation. A bold, semi-autobiographical musical meditation on ambition, excess, and mortality.

A young Indiana cyclist becomes obsessed with training to compete against Italian racing teams in a prestigious local race, much to the amusement and eventual pride of his working-class family. A charming coming-of-age story about dreams, identity, and small-town America.

A Southern textile worker defies her bosses and joins the labor union movement to fight for better conditions in her mill, risking her livelihood and her community's goodwill. A stirring portrait of one woman's awakening courage and determination.

In the aftermath of a family tragedy, a suburban couple struggles to communicate with each other and with their fragile surviving teenage son as he tries to recover from a suicide attempt. A quiet, devastating study of grief, guilt, and the fractures hidden beneath an ordinary family's surface.

The rise and fall of Jake LaMotta, a ferociously talented middleweight boxer whose self-destructive rage ruins his career, his marriages, and his relationships. Martin Scorsese's brutal, black-and-white portrait of a man at war with himself.

The true story of Loretta Lynn, who grew up in poverty in rural Kentucky and became one of country music's biggest stars through raw talent and sheer willpower. Sissy Spacek delivers an acclaimed performance charting Lynn's journey from coal miner's daughter to icon.

In Victorian England, a severely deformed man named Joseph Merrick is rescued from a brutal sideshow and taken in by a compassionate doctor, revealing a gentle and intelligent soul beneath his disfigured exterior. A moving meditation on humanity, dignity, and the cruelty of society.

An adaptation of Thomas Hardy's novel following Tess, a young peasant woman whose life is destroyed by the men who claim to love or own her, set against the sweeping landscapes of 19th-century England. Roman Polanski crafts a lush and tragic portrait of innocence exploited.

Two British athletes — one a devout Christian, one a Jewish sprinter fighting prejudice — prepare for the 1924 Paris Olympics, each driven by deeply personal motivations. An inspiring drama about faith, identity, and the pursuit of glory.

An aging small-time hood forms an unlikely friendship with a young woman in decaying Atlantic City, as they both try to escape their pasts and seize one last chance at something better. A melancholy, beautifully observed film about faded dreams in a city past its prime.

An elderly couple — a retired professor and his sharp-tongued wife — spend a summer at their New England lake house with their adult daughter and son-in-law, confronting old age, estrangement, and the passage of time. Henry Fonda and Katharine Hepburn deliver luminous performances in this tender, bittersweet film.

Archaeologist and adventurer Indiana Jones races against the Nazis to find the legendary Ark of the Covenant before it can be used as a weapon. Steven Spielberg's breathlessly exciting adventure film set the template for modern action blockbusters.

An American journalist and political activist, John Reed, travels to Russia to witness and document the Bolshevik Revolution, while navigating a passionate love affair with writer Louise Bryant. Warren Beatty's epic, ambitious film interweaves personal drama with sweeping historical events.

The life of Mahatma Gandhi is traced from his early days as a lawyer in South Africa through his nonviolent campaign for Indian independence from British rule. Richard Attenborough's sweeping biopic is a monumental tribute to one of history's greatest moral leaders.

A lonely ten-year-old boy befriends a gentle alien accidentally left behind on Earth, and together they work to help the creature phone home before government agents can capture him. Spielberg's beloved classic is a timeless story of friendship, wonder, and the innocence of childhood.

Based on the true story of journalist Charles Horman, an American father searches desperately for his son who disappeared during the violent military coup in Chile in 1973. A gripping political thriller that exposes uncomfortable truths about U.S. government complicity.

A struggling New York actor dresses as a woman to land a soap opera role, then finds the disguise wildly successful — until he falls for his beautiful co-star. A sharp, funny comedy that uses its premise to explore gender roles, honesty, and what it means to truly connect with another person.

A once-great Boston lawyer with a drinking problem takes on a seemingly unwinnable medical malpractice case, seeing it as his last chance for redemption. Sidney Lumet's taut courtroom drama is a masterclass in moral complexity and quiet desperation.

A terminally ill woman reconnects with her estranged daughter and falls for a bumbling astronaut neighbor in this bittersweet dramedy about family, love, and facing death. James L. Brooks balances sharp humor with genuine emotional devastation.

The story of the first American astronauts, from the test pilots who broke the sound barrier to the Mercury Seven who rocketed into space, capturing both their courage and the political machinery that surrounded the space race. A sprawling epic about masculine bravado, competition, and the making of American heroes.

A group of college friends reunite for a weekend after the suicide of a mutual friend, spending a long weekend rediscovering each other, their regrets, and their compromised ideals. A witty, melancholy snapshot of a generation navigating the gap between youthful idealism and adult reality.

An aging Shakespearean actor on his final theatrical tour relies entirely on his devoted dresser to keep him functioning through performance after performance, in a complex relationship built on dependency and unspoken feeling. A beautifully crafted two-hander about art, loyalty, and the end of an era.

A drifting ex-convict finds unexpected peace and purpose in rural Texas when he marries a widow and her young son, struggling to leave his troubled past behind. A quiet, deeply felt drama about grace, redemption, and the possibility of starting over.

In 18th-century Vienna, the mediocre court composer Antonio Salieri is consumed by jealousy and rage toward the divinely gifted — and shockingly vulgar — Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. A dazzling, theatrical exploration of genius, envy, and the cruelty of God's gifts.

An English woman travels to India in the 1920s and becomes entangled in a politically explosive incident when a local doctor is accused of assaulting her in the mysterious Marabar Caves. David Lean's final masterpiece is a rich, layered examination of colonialism and cultural collision.

On a U.S. Army base in 1944, a Black sergeant is found murdered and a Black officer investigates, uncovering buried resentments and tensions within the segregated military. A sharp, psychologically complex murder mystery that doubles as an exploration of race, identity, and power.

In Depression-era Texas, a newly widowed woman struggles to save her family's farm by picking cotton, aided by an unlikely group including a drifter and a blind neighbor. A quiet, deeply moving film about community, endurance, and spiritual grace.

A journalist and his interpreter survive the fall of Cambodia to the Khmer Rouge, only to be separated, with the interpreter left behind to endure the horrors of the killing fields. A devastating, essential film about friendship, survival, and the human cost of war and political violence.

In early 20th-century Kenya, Danish baroness Karen Blixen runs a coffee plantation and falls into a passionate, complicated relationship with the free-spirited hunter Denys Finch Hatton. A lush, elegiac romance about love, loss, and the end of colonial Africa.

A political prisoner in Brazil forms an intimate relationship with his flamboyant cell-mate, a gay man who escapes reality by retelling the plots of old Hollywood films. A provocative, deeply human film about fantasy, freedom, and the bonds formed in confinement.

A hitman falls in love with the woman he is contracted to kill — who happens to be the daughter of a rival mobster — in this darkly comic Mafia satire. John Huston brings a wry, subversive touch to this tale of crime, loyalty, and unlikely romance.

In the American South of the early 1900s, a young Black woman endures decades of hardship, abuse, and separation from her family, while slowly finding her own voice and strength. Spielberg's adaptation of Alice Walker's novel is a powerful, moving portrait of resilience and self-discovery.

A city detective hides in an Amish community after a young boy witnesses a murder, developing a tender romance with a widow while navigating the collision of two radically different worlds. A taut, beautifully observed thriller about violence, pacifism, and belonging.

A young American soldier survives a brutal tour of duty in Vietnam under two clashing sergeants — one humane, one savage — and slowly loses his innocence to the horrors of war. Oliver Stone's visceral, Oscar-winning war film draws on his own combat experience.

A neurotic Manhattan writer juggles his complicated feelings for his ex-wives and current girlfriend while his sister's marriage and happiness take center stage. Woody Allen at his most warm and sophisticated, weaving multiple storylines into a rich, funny, and deeply felt comedy.

In the 16th century, a Jesuit priest undertakes a perilous journey to the South American jungle to build a mission and protect an indigenous community from slave traders. A visually stunning, morally complex film about faith, violence, and the impossibility of grace in a brutal world.

A hearing teacher at a school for the deaf falls in love with a brilliant deaf woman who fiercely refuses to live in the hearing world, creating an impossible romantic conflict. A sensitive, moving drama about communication, pride, and the barriers between two people who love each other.

A repressed English woman travels to Florence with her cousin and has her worldview transformed when she falls for a passionate young Englishman living freely in Italy. A gorgeous Merchant Ivory adaptation of E.M. Forster's novel about social convention, desire, and emotional liberation.

The epic life of Pu Yi, from his childhood as China's last emperor to his imprisonment and re-education as an ordinary citizen under Communist rule. Bernardo Bertolucci's visually breathtaking film is an intimate portrait of a man swept along by the tides of history.

In Washington D.C., a sharp-tongued TV news producer navigates the conflict between her brilliant but unethical anchor and the mediocre but decent reporter she's also falling for. A wickedly smart comedy about the corrupting forces of television and the compromises we make for success.

A happily married New York lawyer's brief affair with a seductive woman turns into a nightmare when she refuses to accept it's over and begins terrorizing his family. A sleek, propulsive psychological thriller that became a cultural touchstone about obsession and infidelity.

A young boy finds adventure and freedom amidst the chaos of the London Blitz during World War II, experiencing the war less as tragedy than as a miraculous disruption of ordinary life. A charming, gently autobiographical film seen entirely through a child's wonder-filled eyes.

A free-spirited Brooklyn woman falls suddenly and irrationally in love with her fiancé's younger brother, setting off a warm, funny, and tender romantic comedy about fate, family, and the moon's mysterious pull. Cher and Nicolas Cage are irresistible in this witty celebration of love's illogic.

An uptight, self-centered Los Angeles businessman is forced to drive his autistic savant brother cross-country after discovering his father left the family fortune to an institution. Barry Levinson's road movie is a funny, touching story about brotherhood, patience, and learning to truly see another person.

Two FBI agents are sent to investigate the disappearance of three civil rights workers in 1964 Mississippi, clashing over methods as they confront a wall of racist silence. A gripping, politically charged thriller about institutional racism and the violent resistance to the civil rights movement.

A grieving travel writer struggling after his wife's death falls for an unconventional woman who slowly draws him back to life, while he writes a book about the world's most boring cities. A quiet, understated romantic drama about emotional paralysis, loss, and the unexpected routes back to feeling.

In pre-revolutionary France, a scheming noblewoman and her equally manipulative former lover play dangerous games of seduction and betrayal among the aristocracy. A lush, wickedly intelligent adaptation of the classic epistolary novel about power, desire, and the cruelty of the privileged class.

A savvy secretary with real business instincts poses as her boss while she's injured and fights to prove that a major corporate deal was actually her idea all along. A sharp, crowd-pleasing comedy about class, ambition, and women navigating a male-dominated workplace.

Over twenty-five years, a crusty retired Southern judge and his Black chauffeur develop an unlikely, evolving friendship as the American South slowly changes around them. A gentle, warmly observed portrait of how prejudice can soften when two people truly learn to see each other.

An inspiring, unconventional English teacher at a prestigious New England boarding school encourages his students to seize the day and think for themselves, with tragic consequences. Peter Weir's beautifully crafted film is a passionate defense of literature, individuality, and the cost of conformity.

movie_title: Born on the Fourth of July
synopsis: Vietnam veteran Ron Kovic, paralyzed from the waist down in combat, returns home to a country that doesn't honor his sacrifice and eventually becomes a leading anti-war activist. Oliver Stone and Tom Cruise create a searing, angry portrait of betrayal, trauma, and political awakening.

An Iowa farmer hears a mysterious voice telling him to build a baseball diamond in his cornfield, setting off a dreamlike journey that ultimately reunites him with the ghost of his estranged father. A gentle, magical film about fathers and sons, second chances, and the timeless pull of the American dream.

The true story of Irish writer Christy Brown, born with severe cerebral palsy, who learned to paint and write using only his left foot and became a celebrated artist despite his disability. Daniel Day-Lewis delivers a ferociously physical and emotional performance in this triumphant story of human will.

A Union soldier who is sent to the frontier alone finds himself living among a Lakota Sioux community, learning their language and customs, and falling in love — before the inevitable clash with an expanding America. Kevin Costner's sweeping, humanist Western is an elegiac tribute to a vanishing way of life.

An aging Michael Corleone tries to legitimize his criminal empire and make peace with his daughter, while a volatile nephew threatens to destroy everything the family has built. A flawed but operatic final chapter to Coppola's legendary Godfather saga.

A doctor in a New York hospital in the 1960s experiments with L-DOPA on long-dormant encephalitis patients, bringing them back to consciousness after decades in a catatonic state — and confronting the heartbreak of what they find. Robin Williams and Robert De Niro deliver moving, nuanced performances in this true story of temporary awakening.

A banker murdered by his corrupt partner returns as a ghost to protect his grieving girlfriend and see his killer brought to justice, with the help of a reluctant psychic. One of the biggest box-office hits of its era, this romantic fantasy became iconic for its pottery scene and Unchained Melody.

The rise and fall of Henry Hill, a low-level New York mobster who lives the glamorous, violent life of the Mafia for decades before becoming an FBI informant. Scorsese's propulsive, definitive gangster film is a dazzling, morally complex celebration and indictment of a criminal world.

An FBI trainee seeks the help of incarcerated cannibal and genius Dr. Hannibal Lecter to catch a serial killer who skins his female victims. One of cinema's most chilling and perfectly constructed thrillers, featuring two of film history's most iconic performances.

In an enchanted kingdom, a young woman is taken prisoner by a cursed Beast and slowly discovers the kind heart beneath his terrifying exterior. Disney's animated masterpiece is a rapturous, timeless romantic fairy tale with unforgettable songs and stunning visuals.

The rise and fall of Benjamin 'Bugsy' Siegel, the charismatic, volatile gangster who dreamed of building a glamorous casino in the Nevada desert and essentially created modern Las Vegas. Warren Beatty is magnetic in this stylish crime drama about ambition, obsession, and mob power.

New Orleans DA Jim Garrison becomes convinced that President Kennedy's assassination was the result of a vast conspiracy, and wages an obsessive decade-long legal crusade to prove it. Oliver Stone's provocative, operatic film is both a compelling thriller and a passionate argument against official history.

A psychiatrist helps a volatile Southern football coach work through the traumatic secrets of his family's past, as the two develop a complicated emotional connection. Barbra Streisand's glossy drama explores memory, repression, and healing with earnest ambition.

An aging outlaw gunslinger agrees to kill two cowboys who cut up a prostitute, joined by his old partner and a young braggart, setting off a chain of brutal consequences. Clint Eastwood's revisionist Western deconstructs the myth of the gunfighter with moral seriousness and violence stripped of glory.

At Guantánamo Bay, a young military lawyer and his partner uncover a possible cover-up reaching the highest levels of the Marine Corps when they defend two soldiers accused of murder. Rob Reiner's courtroom thriller crackles with sharp dialogue and builds to one of cinema's most memorable confrontations.

At the turn of the 20th century, the lives of two families — one wealthy, one striving — become intertwined through commerce, marriage, and class tension in a prosperous English country house. Merchant Ivory's elegant Forster adaptation is a richly detailed meditation on Edwardian England's social divisions.

A retired army lieutenant colonel, blinded in combat and bitter with the world, takes a last wild trip to New York City before planned suicide, accompanied by a prep school student. Al Pacino won the Oscar for his towering, passionate performance in this unlikely friendship story.

A British soldier who falls in love with a mysterious woman in Ireland is drawn into the dangerous world of the IRA, only to discover a shocking secret about his lover's identity. Neil Jordan's film is a tense, tender, and genuinely surprising thriller about love, war, and identity.

The true story of Oskar Schindler, a German industrialist who gradually transforms from war profiteer to unlikely savior, protecting over a thousand Jewish workers from the Holocaust. Spielberg's masterpiece is one of cinema's most important and devastating works.

A wrongly convicted doctor escapes from federal custody and pursues the one-armed man he believes killed his wife, while a relentless U.S. Marshal closes in on him. A supremely entertaining, tightly plotted thriller with Harrison Ford and Tommy Lee Jones at their best.

movie_title: In the Name of the Father
synopsis: Based on the true story of Gerry Conlon, a young Irishman wrongly convicted for an IRA bombing in London and imprisoned for fifteen years, with his father dying in jail beside him. Jim Sheridan's furious, impassioned film is a devastating portrait of injustice and the bond between father and son.

In 1850s New Zealand, a mute Scottish woman is sold in a frontier marriage and must navigate a new life with a stern farmer, while secretly embarking on a passionate affair. Jane Campion's haunting, sensual film explores female desire, silence, and the brutal price of transgression.

The impeccably correct butler of an English country house travels across England to visit a former colleague while reflecting on a life of loyal service — and the emotional repression it required. James Ivory's exquisite adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro's novel is a masterpiece of quiet, devastating understatement.

An intellectually disabled man from Alabama drifts through the most significant events of late 20th-century American history, guided only by his simple goodness and love for his childhood friend Jenny. Robert Zemeckis's wildly popular fable is both a sweeping historical panorama and a tender love story.

Three interlocking stories of violence, crime, and chance in Los Angeles — a pair of small-time robbers, two hitmen on a routine job, and a boxer who refuses to take a dive — told in Tarantino's signature non-linear style. A landmark of 1990s cinema, endlessly quotable and formally dazzling.

A charming but commitment-phobic Englishman attends four weddings and a funeral with his group of eccentric friends, falling repeatedly for the same beautiful American woman. A witty, warm, and endlessly quotable British romantic comedy that made Hugh Grant an international star.

A gentle banker wrongly imprisoned for murder befriends a veteran convict and slowly brings hope and humanity to Shawshank State Prison, while secretly engineering a remarkable plan. Consistently voted among the greatest films ever made, it's a profound story about friendship, hope, and the human spirit.

In 1950s America, a young producer riggs the popular TV quiz show Twenty-One for his telegenic contestant, only for a congressional investigation to unravel the deception. Robert Redford's smart, melancholy film is a meditation on celebrity, integrity, and America's willingness to be deceived.

Scottish warrior William Wallace leads a fierce rebellion against the brutal English king Edward I after the murder of his secret wife, inspiring a nation to fight for freedom. Mel Gibson's sweeping, blood-soaked epic won the Oscar for Best Picture despite — or because of — its operatic historical excesses.

Based on the true story of the Apollo 13 mission, in which a technical malfunction 200,000 miles from Earth forced NASA engineers and three astronauts to improvise a desperate survival plan. Ron Howard's tense, technically masterful film is a celebration of human ingenuity under pressure.

A pig raised on a sheep farm discovers he can herd sheep with kindness rather than intimidation, earning the respect of the farmer and a chance to compete in the Grand National Sheepdog Trials. A charming, witty Australian family film that became a surprise global phenomenon.

On a small Mediterranean island, a young postman becomes close friends with the exiled Chilean poet Pablo Neruda, who teaches him the power of metaphor and helps him woo the woman he loves. A gentle, luminous Italian film about poetry, beauty, and the unexpected ways one person can change another's life.

Two Dashwood sisters — the sensible Elinor and the passionate Marianne — navigate love, heartbreak, and financial hardship in early 19th-century England. Ang Lee's beautiful adaptation of Jane Austen's novel is witty, deeply felt, and anchored by a superb ensemble cast.

A dying patient tells the story of his great wartime love affair — between an English count and a married woman in wartime Italy — to the Canadian nurse caring for him. Anthony Minghella's lush, sweeping romantic epic won nine Oscars for its gorgeous visuals and passionate performances.

In Brainerd, Minnesota, a car salesman hires two criminals to kidnap his wife for ransom money, setting off a catastrophically botched chain of violence investigated by the very pregnant local police chief. The Coen Brothers' darkly comic masterpiece is one of cinema's most perfectly constructed films.

A sports agent is fired for writing an idealistic memo, starts his own agency with only one client and one loyal employee, and fights to survive in a ruthless business while also falling in love. Cameron Crowe's warmhearted film gave the world 'you had me at hello' and 'show me the money.'

A middle-class English woman discovers that a stranger she encounters by chance has a daughter who may be her own child given up for adoption decades earlier, forcing a painful reckoning with secrets and class division. Mike Leigh's Palme d'Or winner is a raw, emotionally shattering examination of truth, shame, and the costs of silence.

The true story of David Helfgott, a gifted Australian pianist who suffers a complete mental breakdown under the pressure of his domineering father and the demands of classical music, then makes an unlikely return to the concert stage. Geoffrey Rush won the Oscar for his extraordinary performance as the fragile, exuberant Helfgott.

Jack and Rose, from opposite ends of the social spectrum, fall deeply in love aboard the doomed RMS Titanic on its maiden voyage in 1912. James Cameron's record-breaking epic is a spectacular disaster film wrapped around one of cinema's most enduring romances.

A janitor at MIT is revealed to be a mathematical genius, and begins working with a professor while also seeing a therapist who helps him confront deep emotional wounds from his past. Matt Damon and Ben Affleck's Oscar-winning script made them stars, and Robin Williams is unforgettable as the compassionate therapist.

A misanthropic, obsessive-compulsive novelist and a depressed single mother form an improbable connection through their unlikely friendship and romantic entanglement. Jack Nicholson and Helen Hunt both won Oscars in this sharp, funny, and surprisingly tender comedy about people who need each other.

In 1950s Los Angeles, a detective investigating a tabloid murder uncovers a vast web of corruption linking the LAPD, Hollywood, and organized crime. Curtis Hanson's neo-noir masterpiece is a rich, morally complex thriller with a stunning ensemble cast.

In a depressed Yorkshire town, a group of unemployed steel workers decide to form a male striptease act to earn money, bonding and finding unexpected self-worth in the process. A warm, funny, and surprisingly moving British comedy about dignity, friendship, and reinvention in the face of economic decline.

In Elizabethan London, a young Shakespeare falls passionately in love with an aristocratic woman who disguises herself as a boy to audition for his new play, inspiring Romeo and Juliet. A witty, romantic, and cleverly constructed comedy that divided critics but charmed audiences worldwide.

The story of the young Queen Elizabeth I consolidating power amid Catholic plots, foreign threats, and her own court's constant maneuvering, all while suppressing her personal desires for the sake of the throne. Cate Blanchett is magnetic in this stylish, politically rich historical drama.

In a World War II Italian concentration camp, a playful Jewish father uses his imagination and humor to shield his young son from the horrors around them, inventing an elaborate fiction that the whole thing is a game. Roberto Benigni's bittersweet fable is one of cinema's most beloved and emotionally shattering films.

Captain Miller leads a squad of soldiers deep behind enemy lines after D-Day to find and bring home a paratrooper whose three brothers have all been killed in the war. Spielberg's brutally realistic war epic opens with the most harrowing D-Day sequence ever committed to film.

Multiple soldiers reflect on life, death, and meaning during the brutal Battle of Guadalcanal in the Pacific, while the natural world around them seems indifferent to their suffering. Terrence Malick's ethereal, philosophical war film is a meditation on nature, violence, and the human capacity for both grace and destruction.

A deeply unhappy suburban father becomes infatuated with his teenage daughter's cheerleader friend, while his wife pursues a real estate rival and their daughter rebels against their hollow lives. Sam Mendes's Oscar-winning debut is a darkly comic and visually ravishing dissection of the American dream's emptiness.

In 1940s Maine, a young orphan works in a cider house operated by a kind doctor who quietly performs illegal abortions, and must eventually confront the moral complexities of the rules he was raised by. Lasse Hallström's gentle adaptation of John Irving's novel is a thoughtful, warmhearted story about choice and compassion.

On Death Row in 1935, a prison guard witnesses the inexplicable healing powers of a gentle giant wrongly convicted of murder, forcing him to question everything he knows about justice and grace. Frank Darabont's emotionally overwhelming supernatural drama is anchored by a towering Michael Clarke Duncan performance.

A tobacco company whistleblower reveals the industry's decades-long conspiracy to suppress research proving cigarettes are deadly, and the journalist who fights to get his story published despite enormous corporate and legal pressure. Michael Mann's taut, morally serious film is one of the best examinations of corporate power and journalistic courage.

A child psychologist working with troubled children takes on the case of a boy who claims to see dead people everywhere he goes, not realizing the truth about his own situation. M. Night Shyamalan's twist-driven thriller became a cultural phenomenon and made Haley Joel Osment a star.

Betrayed by a corrupt Roman senator, Spanish general Maximus escapes slavery, becomes a gladiatorial champion, and plots his revenge against the emperor who murdered his family. Ridley Scott's spectacular, Oscar-winning epic restored the sword-and-sandal epic to cinematic respectability.

A mysterious chocolatier arrives in a rigidly traditional French village during Lent and opens a chocolate shop, gently transforming the lives of its repressed inhabitants. A warm, sensuous fable about pleasure, freedom, and the courage to live fully.

Based on the true story of Erin Brockovich, a single mother and legal clerk who almost single-handedly builds a massive lawsuit against a California energy company poisoning a town's water supply. Julia Roberts won her Oscar with a ferociously energetic and charismatic performance.

Two legendary martial arts warriors pursue a stolen jade sword across imperial China, while a young aristocrat longs to escape her privileged world and become a fighter. Ang Lee's breathtakingly choreographed wuxia epic is both a stunning action spectacle and a meditation on desire and duty.

A DEA agent, a federal judge, and a Mexican policeman each become entangled in America's multibillion-dollar drug war from radically different angles. Soderbergh's multi-stranded, morally unflinching film won four Oscars and remains one of the most honest portraits of the drug trade ever made.

The true story of Nobel Prize-winning mathematician John Nash, who made revolutionary contributions to game theory while battling severe schizophrenia. Ron Howard's emotionally stirring film is anchored by Russell Crowe's committed performance and a powerful twist that reframes everything.

A shooting party at an English country house in 1932 brings together aristocrats and servants whose lives intersect in unexpected and sometimes deadly ways. Robert Altman's witty, densely populated murder mystery is really a subtle meditation on the death throes of the British class system.

movie_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
synopsis: A hobbit named Frodo Baggins inherits a mysterious ring of immense power and sets out on a perilous journey with a diverse fellowship to destroy it in the fires of Mount Doom. Peter Jackson's first installment is a breathtaking achievement in world-building and epic storytelling.

A couple in a small Maine town endure the after-shock of their daughter's murder when the man responsible is released on a technicality, leading to devastating consequences for everyone involved. Todd Field's quiet, devastating debut is a masterwork of slow-burn grief and moral complexity.

A penniless young writer arrives in Paris in 1900 and falls in love with a beautiful courtesan at the Moulin Rouge, even as their secret romance is threatened by a jealous duke. Baz Luhrmann's dazzling, anachronistic musical is a sensory explosion of color, music, and doomed romantic passion.

Chicago, 1920s: a would-be showgirl murders her faithless lover and is defended by a slick lawyer in the middle of a circus-like murder trial, while the true star of the show steals the spotlight. Rob Marshall's electrifying adaptation of the Broadway musical won six Oscars including Best Picture.

Polish-Jewish pianist Władysław Szpilman survives the Nazi occupation of Warsaw by hiding for years in the ruins of the city, helped by a series of strangers including, eventually, a German officer. Roman Polanski's stark, quietly devastating film draws on his own wartime childhood.

In 1860s New York City, Irish immigrant gangs and nativist groups clash violently, and a young man seeks revenge on the powerful gang leader who killed his father. Scorsese's sprawling, visceral epic is both a lurid historical spectacle and a meditation on America's violent origins.

Three women in different eras are all connected by Virginia Woolf's novel Mrs. Dalloway — Woolf herself, a 1950s housewife, and a contemporary editor — all wrestling with depression, conformity, and the cost of living life for others. Stephen Daldry's formally audacious film features three extraordinary lead performances.

movie_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
synopsis: The Fellowship is broken as Frodo and Sam continue their dangerous journey toward Mordor, while Aragorn, Legolas, and Gimli race to save the kingdom of Rohan from Saruman's armies. Peter Jackson's second installment delivers the spectacular Battle of Helm's Deep and deepens the emotional stakes of the entire saga.

movie_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
synopsis: The epic conclusion to Tolkien's saga, as Frodo reaches Mount Doom while Aragorn leads one final desperate battle to distract Sauron and give the Ring-bearer his chance. Peter Jackson's finale swept all eleven of its Oscar categories, a record-equaling achievement.

A jaded American writer meets a young recently-married woman during sleepless nights in a Tokyo hotel, and they form an intimate, undefined connection in a city where they are both profoundly dislocated. Sofia Coppola's quietly beautiful film is a tender study of loneliness, connection, and things left unsaid.

Three friends from a working-class Boston neighborhood are forever marked by a childhood trauma; years later, the murder of one man's daughter draws them all back into each other's lives. Clint Eastwood's devastating crime drama, based on Dennis Lehane's novel, is a wrenching study of fate, guilt, and the wounds that never fully heal.

movie_title: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
synopsis: In 1805, the commanding captain of a British warship pursues a French privateer across the Pacific and around Cape Horn, balancing his friendship with the ship's doctor against his obsessive duty. Peter Weir's richly detailed, strikingly authentic naval epic is one of the best sea films ever made.

The true story of Seabiscuit, a small, overlooked racehorse who became an unlikely champion and a symbol of hope for Depression-era America, told through the lives of the men who believed in him. A crowd-pleasing, emotionally generous film about underdogs, second chances, and the American spirit.

An over-the-hill boxing trainer takes on a determined, talented young woman as his fighter, and a deep bond forms between them as she rises through the ranks — until a catastrophic injury forces an impossible choice. Clint Eastwood's intimate, quietly devastating drama is a love story between a father figure and the fighter who becomes his reason for living.

The true story of Howard Hughes, aviation pioneer and filmmaker, whose obsessive genius gradually curdled into severe mental illness and crippling OCD. Martin Scorsese's glossy, energetic biopic is a showcase for Leonardo DiCaprio's magnetic performance.

Two middle-aged men take a wine-tasting road trip through California wine country before one of them gets married — one desperate for connection and meaning, the other embracing his last week of freedom. Alexander Payne's bittersweet comedy is a beautifully observed portrait of friendship, failure, and the wines we hide behind.

The true story of Ray Charles, the blind Georgia musician who rose from extreme poverty and addiction to become one of America's greatest musical geniuses, revolutionizing R&B, soul, and country. Jamie Foxx's Oscar-winning performance is an uncanny, electrifying tribute.

The story of how playwright J.M. Barrie befriended a widow and her four sons, drawing from his bond with the boys to create Peter Pan and the world of Neverland. A gentle, bittersweet film about imagination, grief, and the need to believe in magic.

After a traffic accident in Los Angeles tangles the lives of people from across the city's racial and social spectrum, simmering tensions and unexpected humanity emerge over two days. Paul Haggis's Oscar-winning ensemble drama about race and connection remains one of the most debated Best Picture winners.

In Wyoming, two young ranch hands hired to tend sheep on a remote mountain fall into a passionate, decades-long secret love affair that neither can escape or fully acknowledge. Ang Lee's heartbreaking film is a masterpiece of restraint and longing.

Truman Capote travels to Kansas to investigate the brutal murder of the Clutter family, and in researching In Cold Blood develops a complex, deeply ambivalent relationship with one of the killers. Philip Seymour Hoffman won the Oscar for his mesmerizing, psychologically nuanced performance.

TV journalist Edward R. Murrow and his CBS team take on Senator Joseph McCarthy during the height of the Red Scare, using McCarthy's own words against him in a series of landmark broadcasts. George Clooney's elegant black-and-white film is both a historical drama and a passionate argument for journalistic courage.

Undercover cop Billy Costigan infiltrates the Boston Irish mob while the mob's own plant inside the police department, Colin Sullivan, works to expose him — creating a tense, lethal game of double-agents spiraling toward catastrophe. Scorsese's Oscar-winning crime thriller is a masterclass in tension, loyalty, and betrayal.

In the aftermath of the 1972 Munich Olympics massacre, the Israeli government dispatches a secret team to assassinate the Palestinian organizers of the attack. Spielberg's morally serious thriller raises uncomfortable questions about revenge, justice, and the human cost of political violence.

Multiple characters on different continents — including a Moroccan family, a pair of Mexican newlyweds, and a deaf-mute Japanese teenager — are connected by the accidental discharge of a rifle. Alejandro González Iñárritu's ambitious ensemble drama explores communication, isolation, and grief across a fractured world.

Told through the letters of Japanese soldiers, the true story of the defense of Iwo Jima from the perspective of the Japanese garrison, including their commanding general who knows the battle is hopeless. Clint Eastwood's companion piece to Flags of Our Fathers is one of the most compassionate war films ever made.

A misfit family — a failed motivational speaker, a suicidal uncle, a mute teenage brother, and a grandfather with a heroin habit — pile into a VW van to drive their youngest member to the Little Miss Sunshine pageant in California. A perfectly calibrated, warmhearted indie comedy about the beauty of a family that fails together.

In the days following the 1997 death of Princess Diana, Queen Elizabeth II is shown navigating the public's overwhelming grief and her family's deeply private mourning, advised by a newly elected Tony Blair. Helen Mirren's extraordinary, Oscar-winning performance finds remarkable humanity in an iconic and famously guarded figure.

A psychopathic hitman and a brutal sheriff pursue a drug dealer across the Texas desert, while a world-weary local lawman contemplates the seemingly inexorable spread of evil. The Coen Brothers' masterpiece is a bleak, masterfully constructed meditation on fate, violence, and mortality.

In turn-of-the-century California, a ruthless, driven oilman builds an empire in the newly discovered oil fields while a conflict with a young evangelical preacher mirrors the raw, violent competition at the heart of American capitalism. Paul Thomas Anderson's ferociously ambitious epic features Daniel Day-Lewis's towering, defining performance.

During World War II, a young English woman's false accusation sends an innocent man to prison and then to war, and she spends her entire adult life trying to understand and atone for her act. Joe Wright's visually stunning adaptation of Ian McEwan's novel is a devastating examination of guilt, memory, and the stories we tell ourselves.

An unconventional teenage girl becomes pregnant and must navigate the decision of what to do, choosing adoption and developing an unexpected friendship with the prospective parents. Diablo Cody's sharp, witty screenplay and Ellen Page's star-making performance make this indie gem both funny and genuinely moving.

An old man is found drifting at sea, mysteriously de-aging as he's taken to a hospital in 2008, and the film traces his entire life backward through the 20th century, from old age to infancy. David Fincher's melancholy, visually sumptuous meditation on time, love, and loss is an American answer to Forrest Gump.

A corporate attorney discovers that his multinational client has been exposed to catastrophic legal liability just before his own life starts to fall apart, as he must decide how far he'll compromise his principles. George Clooney delivers a masterfully controlled performance in this intelligent, morally serious legal thriller.

An Indian orphan from the slums of Mumbai appears on the Indian version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire and is accused of cheating, while a detective uncovers the remarkable true-life stories behind each answer he knew. Danny Boyle's exhilarating, Oscar-sweeping film is a celebration of love, chance, and the life a person can survive.

movie_title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
synopsis: In 1977, TV journalist David Frost negotiates a series of interviews with disgraced former president Richard Nixon, and what follows is a tense psychological chess match between two men with everything to prove. Ron Howard's sharp political drama is built around two remarkable lead performances.

The true story of Harvey Milk, the first openly gay elected official in California history, who built a remarkable political coalition in San Francisco before his assassination. Gus Van Sant's carefully observed, emotionally generous film features Sean Penn's finest performance.

A staff sergeant leading an EOD team in Iraq is revealed to be dangerously addicted to the adrenaline of bomb disposal, unable to function outside the extreme tension of combat. Kathryn Bigelow's taut, Oscar-winning film is a portrait of a man for whom war is the only place he truly feels alive.

In late 1950s Germany, a young woman becomes romantically involved with an older man, only to discover during his war crimes trial that he was a concentration camp guard. Stephen Daldry's adaptation of Bernhard Schlink's novel is a challenging, morally demanding examination of guilt, love, and complicity.

In the future, humanity has destroyed Earth and now lives aboard a massive spaceship while robots clean the abandoned planet; a lonely little waste robot falls in love with a sleek probe and inadvertently triggers the return of the human race. Pixar's visually stunning, nearly wordless sci-fi fable is both a love story and a sharp environmental parable.

Based on the true story of Leigh Anne Tuohy, a strong-willed Tennessee woman who takes in a homeless Black teenager who goes on to become NFL star Michael Oher. A crowd-pleasing, feel-good sports drama that earned Sandra Bullock her Oscar.

In near-future South Africa, an alien spacecraft breaks down above Johannesburg and the alien refugees are forced into a government camp in the city slums, while a bureaucrat tasked with their eviction begins to transform. Neill Blomkamp's viscerally inventive debut uses its sci-fi premise to deliver a sharp allegory about apartheid and xenophobia.

In 1960s London, a precocious schoolgirl is swept off her feet by a charming older man, and begins to question everything her academic education is preparing her for. Carey Mulligan announced herself as a major talent in this nuanced, period-perfect coming-of-age story.

In World War II, a squad of American Jewish soldiers is dropped behind Nazi lines in occupied France with orders to kill as many Germans as possible, as a separate plot to assassinate Hitler takes shape. Tarantino's wildly revisionist, gleefully violent war fantasy is one of his most playful and brilliantly constructed films.

A Jewish physics professor in 1960s Minnesota, whose life seems to be quietly falling apart, consults three rabbis as a series of inexplicable misfortunes befall him, searching for meaning where there may be none. The Coens' bleak, darkly funny philosophical fable is a modern Job story suffused with dread and cosmic indifference.

A widowed balloon salesman ties thousands of balloons to his house and floats away to fulfill his late wife's dream of living by the South American waterfall they saw in a book, accidentally taking a young stowaway with him. Pixar's first ten minutes contain perhaps the most emotionally concentrated storytelling in animation history.

A veteran corporate downsizer who spends most of his life in airports and hotels begins to question his carefully constructed isolation when he falls for a fellow traveler and is saddled with a naive young colleague. Jason Reitman's sharp, melancholy film captures the hollow freedom of the untethered American professional.

An elite New York City ballet dancer's grip on reality begins to disintegrate as she prepares for the dual role of the White and Black Swan in Swan Lake, under the demanding eye of her director. Darren Aronofsky's ferocious psychological horror is a breathtaking portrait of perfection as self-destruction.

A morbidly obese, barely literate Black teenager from Harlem is discovered to be pregnant with her second child by her abusive father, and is placed in an alternative school where a dedicated teacher begins to unlock her intelligence and spirit. An unflinching, deeply moving portrait of survival, told with raw honesty.

King George VI, crippled by a severe stammer, reluctantly begins working with an unorthodox Australian speech therapist as Britain prepares for World War II, forming an unlikely and transformative friendship. A beautifully crafted, deeply humanist film built on two extraordinary performances by Colin Firth and Geoffrey Rush.

In 1970s Boston, a drug-addicted boxer makes a miraculous comeback with the help of his half-brother trainer, while navigating a controlling mother and a new girlfriend who demands he take control of his life. David O. Russell's crackling ensemble film features extraordinary work from Christian Bale and Melissa Leo.

A skilled thief specializing in planting ideas in people's dreams is hired to perform the most complex job of all: inception — planting an idea so deep in a target's mind he believes it was his own. Christopher Nolan's elaborately constructed sci-fi thriller is a cerebral, visually spectacular puzzle box.

Two married women — one a biology professor, the other her longtime partner's ex-wife — have their orderly lesbian household disrupted when their two teenage children track down the sperm donor who is their biological father. A warm, witty, and beautifully observed comedy-drama about modern family structures and the complexities of parenting.

Mountain climber Aron Ralston is trapped alone in a Utah canyon when a boulder falls on his arm, and spends 127 hours trying to survive before making an impossible choice. Danny Boyle turns a one-man survival story into an electrifying, surprisingly life-affirming piece of filmmaking.

The founding of Facebook is traced through the depositions of two separate lawsuits, as the friendless, socially abrasive Mark Zuckerberg creates the world's most powerful social network and in doing so betrays the only friends he had. David Fincher and Aaron Sorkin's film crackles with wit and moral complexity.

Woody, Buzz, and the rest of Andy's toys face being given away as Andy heads to college, leading them to a terrifying adventure through a day-care center before a climactic farewell. Pixar's achievement in delivering genuine emotional closure to a beloved franchise remains one of animation's crowning moments.

In the harsh winter Ozarks, a teenage girl searches for her missing meth-cooking father to save the family home, navigating the dangerous, closed world of her rural community. Debra Granik's atmospheric, fiercely unsentimental film announced Jennifer Lawrence as one of the great young actors of her generation.

A seventeen-year-old girl in the Ozark Mountains searches for her missing meth-cooking father to prevent the family from losing their home, navigating the dangerous, closed world of her rural community. Debra Granik's atmospheric, fiercely unsentimental film announced Jennifer Lawrence as one of the great young actors of her generation.

In Hollywood, 1927, a silent film star and his studio refuse to embrace the coming of sound, while a young actress he discovers becomes a massive star of talking pictures. Michel Hazanavicius's charming, genuinely cinephilic homage to silent cinema is shot in black-and-white with a virtually silent soundtrack.

A nine-year-old boy in New York, still traumatized two years after losing his father in the 9/11 attacks, discovers a mysterious key in a vase in his father's closet and embarks on a quest across the five boroughs to find what it opens. Stephen Daldry's divisive adaptation of Jonathan Safran Foer's novel is heartfelt if occasionally over-wrought.

A recently divorced Hawaii land baron must reconnect with his two daughters following his wife's accident, while learning to grieve and to confront secrets about her life he didn't know. Alexander Payne's beautifully observed dramedy features George Clooney's most emotionally generous performance.

In 1960s Mississippi, a young white woman writes a book from the perspective of the Black maids who raised the white families of Jackson, risking the wrath of the community. Tate Taylor's crowd-pleasing adaptation of Kathryn Stockett's novel features powerful performances from Viola Davis and Octavia Spencer.

A young boy in 1930s Paris discovers a secret hidden in the walls of the Gare Montparnasse railway station, which leads him to the forgotten legacy of pioneering filmmaker Georges Méliès. Scorsese's loving tribute to early cinema is also a visually gorgeous, emotionally tender mystery adventure.

The true story of Billy Beane, the Oakland Athletics general manager who revolutionized baseball by building a competitive team through statistical analysis rather than traditional scouting. Bennett Miller's film makes the economics of baseball compulsively watchable through Brad Pitt's charismatic, quietly sad performance.

A nostalgic American writer in Paris discovers he can travel back in time to the 1920s at midnight, meeting his literary heroes — and confronting the truth that everyone romanticizes a golden age they didn't live in. Woody Allen's most purely enchanting film in decades is a gentle, witty meditation on nostalgia and the present.

A Texas family's life — parents' tumultuous marriage, a son's death, and the eldest child's adult memories of childhood — are woven together with cosmic images of the origin of the universe. Terrence Malick's audacious, rapturous film is one of the most formally ambitious ever made, dividing audiences between devotion and bewilderment.

During World War I, a young English soldier named Albert forms a powerful bond with a horse named Joey before the animal is sold to the cavalry and sent to the front, and Albert follows to find him. Spielberg's sweeping, old-fashioned epic is a tribute to the heroism of animals and the soldiers who loved them.

The true story of how CIA officer Tony Mendez rescued six American diplomats hiding in revolutionary Iran in 1980 by creating an elaborate fake Canadian film production as their cover. Ben Affleck's tightly wound thriller is a masterclass in suspense-building, culminating in a breathtaking airport sequence.

In the final months of the Civil War, Abraham Lincoln uses every political tool at his disposal to push the Thirteenth Amendment abolishing slavery through a resistant House of Representatives. Spielberg's film is really a sophisticated political procedural, powered by Daniel Day-Lewis's magisterial, authoritative performance.

The inside story of the decade-long CIA hunt for Osama bin Laden, focused on a relentless female analyst who becomes convinced of the intelligence that leads to the Abbottabad raid. Kathryn Bigelow's controlled, procedural thriller sparked intense debate about torture's role in the hunt.

Victor Hugo's epic musical follows the ex-convict Jean Valjean across decades of French history, as he reinvents himself and cares for the illegitimate daughter of a dying factory worker, while relentlessly pursued by the implacable Inspector Javert. Tom Hooper's live-sung adaptation is ambitious if visually claustrophobic.

A bipolar man moves back in with his parents after a stint in a psychiatric hospital and becomes friends with a woman with her own mental health issues, culminating in an unexpected ballroom dance competition. David O. Russell's energetic, warmhearted romantic comedy earned Oscar nominations for all four lead actors.

In the antebellum South, a freed Black man is captured and sold back into slavery, and a German bounty hunter offers to help him find and free his wife in exchange for help tracking down criminals. Tarantino's wildly entertaining, deliberately provocative revisionist Western uses genre conventions to explore slavery with fury and dark humor.

In Vienna, an elderly couple whose lives are entirely intertwined face the aftermath of the wife's devastating stroke, as the husband cares for her at home with fierce, exhausted love. Michael Haneke's austere, devastating film is one of cinema's most honest portrayals of aging, caregiving, and the end of love.

In the Louisiana bayou, a six-year-old girl named Hushpuppy lives with her ailing father in a ramshackle community threatened by rising floodwaters, while ancient aurochs awaken in her imagination. Benh Zeitlin's lyrical debut is a miraculous, elemental film shot with the force of myth and anchored by an extraordinary child performance.

After a terrible storm sinks his ship, a teenage Indian boy is left stranded in the Pacific on a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger, and must learn to coexist with the animal to survive. Ang Lee's visually astonishing adaptation of Yann Martel's novel is a meditation on storytelling, faith, and the stories we need to survive.

When their spacecraft is damaged by debris, two astronauts are left adrift in Earth's orbit with dwindling oxygen and no way home. Alfonso Cuarón's technically breathtaking film is both a survival thriller and a meditation on grief, isolation, and the will to live.

In 1970s New Jersey, a team of con artists — led by a charming scammer and his gifted partner — are coerced by an FBI agent into running an elaborate sting targeting corrupt politicians. David O. Russell's dazzling ensemble comedy is a riotous celebration of style, deception, and the art of reinvention.

The true story of Ron Woodroof, a Texas electrician who tests HIV-positive in 1985 and begins smuggling experimental and unapproved drugs into the U.S. to treat himself and fellow patients, founding the Dallas Buyers Club. Matthew McConaughey and Jared Leto both won Oscars for their physically transformative, deeply felt performances.

A lonely, introverted writer in near-future Los Angeles falls in love with his newly installed, disarmingly warm operating system, and discovers that their relationship challenges every assumption he has about connection and consciousness. Spike Jonze's tender, melancholy film is one of the most thoughtful love stories of the digital age.

The true story of Philomena Lee, an elderly Irish woman who spent fifty years searching for the son she was forced to give up for adoption as a teenager by nuns, aided by a disgraced journalist writing her story. Judi Dench and Steve Coogan are perfectly matched in this compassionate, quietly angry story about faith, loss, and forgiveness.

The rise and fall of Jordan Belfort, a New York stockbroker who built a fraudulent empire of greed, drugs, sex, and crime before his inevitable arrest. Scorsese's delirious, three-hour excess machine features Leonardo DiCaprio's most uninhibited performance and became notorious for its record-breaking profanity count.

Based on Solomon Northup's memoir, the true story of a free Black man in antebellum New York who is kidnapped and sold into slavery in Louisiana, spending twelve years trying to survive and return to his family. Steve McQueen's unflinching, morally serious film is one of the most important American films ever made about slavery.

An elderly Nebraska man insists on driving from Montana to Nebraska to collect what he believes is a million-dollar sweepstakes prize, and his estranged son accompanies him on the journey, slowly learning about his father's hidden life. Alexander Payne's tender, black-and-white road movie is a quietly devastating portrait of fathers, sons, and American decline.

The true story of Captain Richard Phillips, whose container ship is seized by Somali pirates in the Indian Ocean in 2009. Paul Greengrass's taut, procedural thriller builds to a final act of extraordinary, devastating power.

Based on the memoir of Navy SEAL Chris Kyle, the deadliest sniper in American military history, whose four tours in Iraq and 160 confirmed kills were matched by a disintegrating family life and severe PTSD. Clint Eastwood's divisive, box-office phenomenon is a sincere portrait of a complicated man and the costs of war.

Filmed over twelve years with the same cast, the life of a Texas boy named Mason is traced from childhood through college, capturing the texture of growing up in real time. Richard Linklater's formally unprecedented film is both an extraordinary cinematic experiment and a deeply felt portrait of an ordinary American life.

A young concierge at the legendary Grand Budapest Hotel in the 1930s finds himself entangled in a murder mystery and a chase involving a priceless painting, guided by the hotel's impeccable and eccentric chief concierge. Wes Anderson's most purely entertaining film is a dazzling confection of wit, style, and unexpected melancholy.

A faded Hollywood superhero actor mounts a comeback by writing and starring in a Broadway play, while the spirit of his famous character whispers in his ear and his production spirals toward chaos. Alejandro González Iñárritu's audacious, apparently one-take film is a savage, compassionate dissection of artistic ego and the hunger for relevance.

The story of Martin Luther King Jr.'s historic 1965 voting rights marches from Selma to Montgomery, and the political maneuvering between King and President Lyndon Johnson. Ava DuVernay's powerful historical drama captures both the strategic brilliance of the civil rights movement and the vicious violence it faced.

The true story of Alan Turing, the mathematical genius who cracked the Nazi Enigma code and helped win World War II, while hiding his homosexuality in a Britain where it was a criminal offense. Benedict Cumberbatch's nuanced performance anchors this gripping drama about genius, injustice, and the cost of secrecy.

A driven young jazz drummer is accepted into a prestigious music conservatory and begins working under a brilliant, ferociously demanding conductor who uses psychological abuse as a teaching tool. Damien Chazelle's intensely crafted film is both a riveting musical thriller and a troubling meditation on the relationship between greatness and cruelty.

The true story of the early relationship between physicist Stephen Hawking and his first wife Jane, from their courtship at Cambridge through his diagnosis with motor neurone disease to his rise to world fame. A beautifully acted, emotionally generous film that focuses as much on Jane's sacrifices as on Hawking's genius.

The true story of the Boston Globe's investigative Spotlight team, who uncovered the systematic sexual abuse of children by Catholic priests and the Church's decades-long cover-up of the crimes. Tom McCarthy's measured, devastating ensemble film is a model of serious journalism depicted on screen.

In 1820s Montana, fur trapper Hugh Glass is mauled by a bear and left for dead by his hunting party — including the man who kills his son — and survives a brutal winter wilderness to pursue his revenge. Alejandro G. Iñárritu's physically punishing, visually magnificent film is an endurance test about survival and grief.

The true story of the 2008 financial crisis, explained through the experiences of the small group of outsiders who foresaw the collapse of the US housing market and bet against it. Adam McKay's bold, formally inventive film makes the arcane mechanics of financial catastrophe both comprehensible and infuriating.

An astronaut is accidentally left behind on Mars when his crew evacuates during a storm, and must use his botanical and engineering skills to survive until a rescue mission can reach him. Ridley Scott's warm, problem-solving survival film is an optimistic celebration of human ingenuity.

A young woman is abducted and raised in a garden shed by a disturbed man, becoming the only world her young son has ever known, until she decides they must attempt a desperate escape. Lenny Abrahamson's extraordinary film is told entirely from the boy's innocent perspective, making its horrors and its wonders equally real.

The true story of lawyer James Donovan, who negotiated the exchange of captured American pilot Gary Powers for Soviet spy Rudolf Abel at the height of the Cold War. Spielberg and Tom Hanks deliver an intelligent, classically crafted Cold War thriller about integrity, duty, and the meaning of the rule of law.

In the 1950s, a young Irish woman emigrates to Brooklyn, where she finds a new life and a new love — until news from home summons her back and forces a heartbreaking choice. John Crowley's exquisitely crafted, deeply moving film is a portrait of the immigrant experience told with grace and precision.

In a post-apocalyptic desert wasteland, an enslaved warrior and a group of women he's helping to escape pursue a desperate high-speed flight from a tyrannical warlord across the wasteland, with an entire army in pursuit. George Miller's visceral, inventive action spectacle is also a surprisingly coherent feminist myth about captivity and freedom.

A young Black man growing up in Miami is shown in three chapters of his life — as a shy, bullied child, a vulnerable teenager, and a hardened young adult — each illuminating the forces shaping his identity and sexuality. Barry Jenkins's luminous, tender film is one of the great coming-of-age films and a landmark of LGBTQ+ cinema.

A struggling jazz pianist and an aspiring actress fall in love in contemporary Los Angeles, supporting each other's dreams as the realities of adult life and ambition slowly pull them apart. Damien Chazelle's stunning musical tribute to Hollywood's golden age is both a joyful celebration of dreaming and a bittersweet meditation on love and compromise.

A working-class Boston man returns to his hometown to care for his nephew after his brother's death, and must confront the devastating loss that caused him to leave years before. Kenneth Lonergan's magnificent, gut-wrenching film is one of the most honest portrayals of grief and the limits of recovery ever filmed.

In 1950s Pittsburgh, an African-American garbage man and former baseball player confronts the constraints placed on his life by racism, as tensions within his family come to a head in one tumultuous week. Denzel Washington's powerful adaptation of August Wilson's Pulitzer Prize-winning play is raw, theatrical, and devastating.

When a mysterious alien signal offers humanity a terrifying message, a linguist is recruited by the military to communicate with the visitors before global panic triggers catastrophic conflict. Denis Villeneuve's elegant, profound sci-fi film uses its premise to meditate on language, time, loss, and how we choose to live knowing what we know.

The true story of Desmond Doss, a Seventh-day Adventist and conscientious objector who refused to carry a weapon but served as a combat medic in the Pacific, single-handedly saving 75 men at the Battle of Hacksaw Ridge. Mel Gibson's brutal, emotionally overwhelming war film is a tribute to one of the war's most extraordinary acts of courage.

Two bank-robbing brothers terrorize West Texas, pursued by a weary Texas Ranger, while a complex relationship develops between one brother and the local banker he's extorting. David Mackenzie's sun-scorched neo-Western is a tense, beautifully acted story about poverty, desperation, and the violence of economic inequality.

The true story of three Black female mathematicians at NASA — Katherine Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan, and Mary Jackson — whose extraordinary calculations were essential to the success of the early American space program, even as they fought against segregation and sexism. A crowd-pleasing, important feel-good film about unsung heroes.

The true story of Saroo Brierley, an Indian boy who is separated from his family and adopted by an Australian couple, who twenty-five years later uses Google Earth to find his way back to his birth mother. A deeply moving, crowd-pleasing story about family, belonging, and the remarkable persistence of memory.

In Cold War Baltimore, a mute cleaning woman working at a secret government laboratory discovers and befriends an amphibious humanoid creature, and falls into a tender, impossible romance. Guillermo del Toro's visually ravishing romantic fantasy is a tribute to the power of love between outsiders.

In a small Missouri town, a woman puts up three billboards challenging the local sheriff's failure to solve her daughter's murder, setting off an escalating war of anger, grief, and dark, unexpected comedy. Martin McDonagh's fierce, brilliant, morally generous film refuses to let any of its characters be simply villains.

In May 1940, 400,000 Allied troops are trapped on the beach at Dunkirk as the German army closes in, and the story of their evacuation is told simultaneously from land, sea, and air. Christopher Nolan's masterpiece of pure cinema is an overwhelming, nearly dialogue-free experience of survival under impossible pressure.

A sharp-tongued, self-possessed Sacramento teenager navigates her senior year — applying to colleges, falling for boys, fighting with her mother, and slowly realizing how much she loves the home she's desperate to leave. Greta Gerwig's directorial debut is perfectly observed, deeply funny, and surprisingly moving.

A young Black man visits his white girlfriend's parents at their secluded estate and realizes, with mounting dread, that something deeply sinister is happening to the Black people in this community. Jordan Peele's brilliant debut is simultaneously a masterfully constructed horror film and a sharp, unsettling allegory about race in liberal America.

The true story of how Washington Post publisher Katharine Graham and editor Ben Bradlee defied government pressure and the threat of prosecution to publish the Pentagon Papers, exposing decades of government lies about the Vietnam War. Spielberg's swift, principled film is a celebration of a free press and the courage it requires.

In the summer of 1983 in northern Italy, seventeen-year-old Elio falls into an intense, passionate, and complicated love with Oliver, his father's twenty-four-year-old graduate student. Luca Guadagnino's sun-drenched, achingly beautiful film captures the bittersweet intensity of first love with extraordinary delicacy.

In 1950s London, a masterful couturier creates exquisite dresses for socialites and royalty while his carefully controlled life is disrupted by a sharp-witted waitress who refuses to play by his rules. Paul Thomas Anderson's gorgeously crafted psychological drama is a strange, unsettling, and deeply romantic study of creative obsession.

The true story of Winston Churchill's first weeks as Prime Minister in May 1940, when he faced enormous pressure to negotiate a peace treaty with Hitler while secretly considering whether to fight on alone. Gary Oldman's transformative, Oscar-winning performance is the centerpiece of this gripping historical drama.

The true story of Tony Lip, a working-class Italian-American bouncer from the Bronx who becomes the driver for Dr. Don Shirley, a refined and brilliant Black pianist, on a concert tour through the segregated Deep South in 1962. Peter Farrelly's crowd-pleasing odd-couple film won Best Picture amid considerable controversy.

A year in the life of Cleo, a domestic worker for a middle-class family in Mexico City in the early 1970s, as she navigates an unexpected pregnancy while the family around her faces its own quiet crisis. Alfonso Cuarón's deeply personal, visually stunning black-and-white film is a tribute to the women who raised him.

In 18th-century England, the ailing Queen Anne is manipulated by her scheming favorite Lady Sarah, whose position is threatened when a newcomer cousin arrives at court and begins competing for the Queen's affection. Yorgos Lanthimos's darkly comic, brilliantly performed film is a savage portrait of power, dependency, and cruelty.

A country music star and an aspiring singer meet and fall in love during a tumultuous concert tour, even as her star rises and his personal demons threaten to destroy them both. Bradley Cooper's directorial debut is a visually assured, emotionally raw remake anchored by his chemistry with Lady Gaga.

In 1970s Colorado, Black detective Ron Stallworth infiltrates the Ku Klux Klan by phone while his white Jewish partner poses as him in person, in an operation stranger and more disturbing than any fiction. Spike Lee's furious, funny, and formally inventive film uses history to skewer the present.

The story of Freddie Mercury and Queen, from their early days playing London pubs to their triumphant Live Aid performance in 1985, focusing on Mercury's flamboyant genius and his personal struggles with identity and illness. Rami Malek won the Oscar in a bold, physically committed performance at the center of this crowd-pleasing but critically divisive biopic.

The political rise and fall of Dick Cheney, traced from a dissolute young man in Wyoming to the most powerful and secretive Vice President in American history. Adam McKay's formally anarchic, sharply angry film is a satirical portrait of how quiet men accumulate and abuse power.

Prince T'Challa returns to Wakanda to assume the throne after his father's death, but his right to rule is challenged by a formidable enemy with a legitimate grievance and a plan to weaponize Wakanda's technology. Ryan Coogler's culturally landmark superhero film celebrates African identity with extraordinary visual richness.

A con-man father and his scheming family attempt to infiltrate a wealthy Seoul household by getting jobs as their housekeeper and tutor, until a shocking secret beneath the house upends their plans with dark consequences. Bong Joon Ho's perfectly crafted thriller is a devastating parable about class inequality.

Aging hitman Frank Sheeran reflects on his decades working for the Teamsters union and his relationship with Jimmy Hoffa, claiming responsibility for Hoffa's disappearance. Scorsese's elegiac, three-and-a-half-hour gangster film uses digital de-aging technology to trace the moral and physical costs of a life of violence.

In April 1917, two young British soldiers are ordered to cross enemy lines and personally deliver a message that could prevent 1,600 men from walking into a deadly ambush. Sam Mendes's technical masterpiece — shot to appear as a single continuous take — is an immersive, terrifying journey through the Western Front.

Arthur Fleck, a failed Gotham City comedian with mental illness, is pushed over the edge by relentless humiliation and social neglect, transforming into the anarchic criminal known as the Joker. Todd Phillips's dark, divisive origin story is carried by Joaquin Phoenix's extraordinary, risk-taking performance.

movie_title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
synopsis: In 1969 Hollywood, fading TV star Rick Dalton and his stuntman best friend navigate a changing industry, while their neighbor Sharon Tate and the Manson Family orbit each other in the months before the murders. Tarantino's love letter to an era is a leisurely, funny, deeply melancholy film about obsolescence and the power of friendship.

The true story of the 1966 Le Mans race, in which Ford Motor Company tasked car designer Carroll Shelby and racing driver Ken Miles to build a car capable of defeating Ferrari. James Mangold's thrilling, exceptionally well-crafted racing film is also a story about creative independence in the face of corporate bureaucracy.

A couple going through a painful divorce in New York — both theatre professionals — navigate custody of their young son while their lawyers formalize the end of a marriage still full of love. Noah Baumbach's most emotionally raw film is a devastating, compassionate examination of how two people who love each other can still hurt each other terribly.

A ten-year-old boy in Nazi Germany is raised by the fanatical JoJo Bauer, who idolizes an imaginary Hitler, until he discovers that his mother is hiding a Jewish girl in their house. Taika Waititi's audacious anti-hate satire somehow makes comedy and heartbreak coexist in a film about the absurdity and evil of fascism.

Louisa May Alcott's beloved novel about the four March sisters — Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy — growing up in Civil War-era Massachusetts is given a formally inventive adaptation that moves fluidly between timelines. Greta Gerwig's film honors its source material while making a quietly radical argument about women's lives and creative autonomy.

A recently widowed woman joins a community of nomadic Americans living in vans, traveling through the American West from seasonal job to seasonal job, and finding an unexpected sense of freedom and belonging. Chloé Zhao's quiet, observational film stars Frances McDormand in an almost wordless performance of extraordinary grace.

The true story of Fred Hampton, the charismatic young chairman of the Black Panther Party's Illinois chapter, and the FBI informant Bill O'Neal who infiltrated the organization and helped engineer Hampton's assassination at age twenty-one. Shaka King's fierce, politically passionate film is one of the essential American films about race and power.

The true story of the trial of seven political protesters charged with inciting a riot during the 1968 Democratic National Convention in Chicago, in a courtroom that became a theater of radical democracy. Aaron Sorkin's propulsive, superbly acted drama is both a historical lesson and a passionate argument for protest.

A young woman who was date-raped in college poses as a party-girl medical student years later, systematically identifying and confronting the men who assault vulnerable women at parties. Emerald Fennell's sharp, deeply unsettling film uses genre conventions to explore rape culture, survivor trauma, and the limits of justice.

A heavy metal drummer begins losing his hearing and, while on tour in Europe, is placed in a drug and alcohol rehabilitation program, where he must confront who he is without the music that defines him. Darius Marder's restrained, beautifully crafted film uses sound design as a formal tool to put us inside its protagonist's experience.

The story of Herman J. Mankiewicz, the witty, self-destructive screenwriter who wrote the script for Citizen Kane in 1940, told in the style of the classic film he was creating. David Fincher's love letter to Hollywood's Golden Age is a gorgeous, complex, and deeply personal film.

An elderly man with dementia slowly loses his grip on his identity and his surroundings, while his daughter struggles to care for him. Florian Zeller's formally audacious adaptation of his own play puts us inside a deteriorating mind with shattering effectiveness, anchored by Anthony Hopkins's extraordinary Oscar-winning performance.

A Korean-American family moves from California to a rural Arkansas farm to build the life the father has always dreamed of, as the grandmother arrives from Korea and disrupts the domestic order. Lee Isaac Chung's tender, semi-autobiographical film is a deeply felt portrait of immigrant dreams, family love, and the American soil.

A CODA — Child of Deaf Adults — must choose between staying to support her deaf family's fishing business or pursuing her gift for singing at a prestigious music conservatory. Sian Heder's warm, crowd-pleasing film is elevated by the extraordinary performances of its deaf cast members.

A renowned Japanese stage director processes the recent death of his wife by staging Uncle Vanya with his theatre company, and embarks on a three-month road trip with a widowed actress from the cast. Ryusuke Hamaguchi's three-hour masterwork is a profound meditation on grief, language, art, and how we give our feelings to others.

In 1970s San Fernando Valley, a fifteen-year-old girl and a twenty-five-year-old waterbed salesman have an unlikely, meandering non-romance as they orbit the edges of the film industry and fall in and out of each other's lives. Paul Thomas Anderson's shaggy, affectionate ode to the Valley is a film about the texture of a place and a time.

On the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the universe's most valuable substance, young Paul Atreides and his family are given control of the treacherous spice trade, setting off a deadly political conflict. Denis Villeneuve's magnificent, awe-inspiring adaptation of Frank Herbert's science fiction epic is one of the great world-building films.
